medications.name: Acetaminophen (Tylenol)
medications.shortDescription: Over-the-counter pain reliever and fever reducer
medications.description: Acetaminophen is an over-the-counter medication used to relieve mild to moderate pain and reduce fever. It works by reducing substances in the body that cause pain and fever.
medications.howToUse: Take by mouth with or without food. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water.
medications.dosage: Adults: 325-650 mg every 4-6 hours, not to exceed 3,000-4,000 mg per day. Children: Dosage based on weight.
medications.seriousSideEffects: Severe liver damage can occur with overdose or chronic use of high doses. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, or severe abdominal pain.
medications.drugInteractions: May interact with warfarin and other blood thinners. Avoid alcohol as it increases risk of liver damage.
precautions: Do not exceed recommended daily dose
Avoid if you have liver disease
Use with caution if you drink alcohol regularly
Tell doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding

medications.name: Ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin)
medications.shortDescription: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) for pain and inflammation
medications.description: Ibuprofen is an over-the-counter NSAID that reduces pain, fever, and inflammation. It blocks prostaglandins that cause pain and inflammation in the body.
medications.howToUse: Take by mouth with food or milk to reduce stomach upset. Swallow tablets whole with water.
medications.dosage: Adults: 200-400 mg every 4-6 hours as needed, not to exceed 1,200 mg per day without doctor supervision.
medications.seriousSideEffects: May cause stomach bleeding, particularly with long-term use. Increased risk of heart attack or stroke. Seek medical attention if you experience black/tarry stools, vomiting blood, or chest pain.
medications.drugInteractions: May interact with blood pressure medications, blood thinners, and other NSAIDs. Do not combine with other NSAIDs.
precautions: Do not use if you have ulcers or bleeding disorders
Use with caution if you have heart disease or high blood pressure
Avoid during pregnancy, especially the third trimester
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving if affected

medications.name: Amoxicillin
medications.shortDescription: Penicillin-type antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections
medications.description: Amoxicillin is a penicillin-type antibiotic that kills bacteria or stops their growth. It is used to treat various bacterial infections.
medications.howToUse: Take by mouth with or without food. Take exactly as prescribed for the full course, even if you feel better.
medications.dosage: Adults: Typically 250-500 mg every 8 hours or 500-875 mg every 12 hours. Children: Dosage based on weight.
medications.seriousSideEffects: Severe allergic reactions including anaphylaxis (difficulty breathing, swelling of face/throat). Severe diarrhea (C. difficile infection). Seek immediate medical attention if these occur.
medications.drugInteractions: May reduce effectiveness of birth control pills. Can interact with methotrexate. May interact with warfarin (blood thinner).
precautions: Do not use if you are allergic to penicillin or cephalosporins
Tell your doctor about all medications you are taking
Complete the full course of antibiotics
May cause false positive in pregnancy tests

medications.name: Cetirizine (Zyrtec)
medications.description: Cetirizine is a second-generation antihistamine that provides relief from allergy symptoms by blocking histamine receptors without significantly crossing the blood-brain barrier.
uses: Relieving itchy, watery eyes from allergies
medications.howToUse: Take by mouth with or without food. Swallow tablets whole or dissolve on tongue.
medications.dosage: Adults: 5-10 mg once daily, preferably in the evening. Children 6-11 years: 5 mg once daily.
medications.seriousSideEffects: Severe allergic reactions (rare). Hallucinations or psychiatric effects (very rare). Seek medical attention if symptoms develop.
medications.drugInteractions: May interact with alcohol (increased drowsiness) and anticholinergic drugs. Generally safe with most other medications.
precautions: Use with caution when driving due to potential drowsiness
Do not use if allergic to cetirizine or hydroxyzine
Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease
Avoid alcohol as it may increase drowsiness

medications.name: Diphenhydramine (Benadryl)
medications.description: Diphenhydramine is a first-generation antihistamine that crosses the blood-brain barrier, causing drowsiness. It's used for allergies and as a sleep aid.
medications.howToUse: Take by mouth with or without food. Do not chew tablets; swallow whole.
medications.dosage: Adults: 25-50 mg every 4-6 hours as needed, not to exceed 300 mg per day. Children 6-11 years: 12.5-25 mg every 4-6 hours.
medications.seriousSideEffects: Severe allergic reactions (rare). Confusion or hallucinations (especially in elderly). Rapid heartbeat. Seek medical attention if concerning symptoms develop.
medications.drugInteractions: Do not combine with alcohol or other CNS depressants. May interact with anticholinergic medications. Not recommended with MAOI inhibitors.
precautions: Use with caution when driving or operating machinery
Do not use in children under 2 years without doctor supervision
Avoid alcohol
Use with caution if you have glaucoma or heart problems

medications.name: Cough Syrup with Dextromethorphan (Robitussin)
medications.description: Dextromethorphan is an over-the-counter cough suppressant that reduces the urge to cough by acting on the cough center in the brain.
uses: Reducing cough from upper respiratory infections
medications.howToUse: Take by mouth as directed on the package. Do not exceed recommended dose.
medications.dosage: Adults: 10-20 mg every 4-6 hours, not to exceed 120 mg per day. Children 6-11 years: 5-10 mg every 4-6 hours, not to exceed 60 mg per day.
medications.seriousSideEffects: Abuse potential at high doses (euphoric effects). Can cause serotonin syndrome if combined with certain medications. Seek medical attention if confusion or hallucinations occur.
medications.drugInteractions: Do not combine with MAOI inhibitors. May interact with SSRIs and other serotonergic drugs. Alcohol increases risk of side effects.
precautions: Do not exceed recommended dose
Do not use for productive cough (cough with phlegm)
Avoid if you have had recent MAOI use
May cause drowsiness; do not drive if affected

medications.name: Pseudoephedrine (Sudafed)
medications.shortDescription: Decongestant for nasal and sinus congestion
medications.description: Pseudoephedrine is a decongestant that constricts blood vessels in the nasal passages, reducing swelling and congestion.
medications.howToUse: Take by mouth with or without food. Swallow tablets whole. Do not crush or chew.
medications.dosage: Adults: 30-60 mg every 4-6 hours, not to exceed 240 mg per day. Children 6-11 years: 30 mg every 4-6 hours, not to exceed 120 mg per day.
medications.seriousSideEffects: May cause elevated blood pressure, especially in people with hypertension. Increased heart rate or chest pain. Seek medical attention if these occur.
medications.drugInteractions: Do not combine with MAOI inhibitors or decongestants. May interact with blood pressure medications and some antidepressants.
precautions: Do not use if you have high blood pressure without doctor approval
Avoid if you have heart disease or thyroid disease
Do not use if taking MAOI inhibitors
May increase nervousness or insomnia; avoid taking in evening

medications.name: Lisinopril
medications.shortDescription: ACE inhibitor for blood pressure management
medications.description: Lisinopril is an ACE inhibitor that relaxes blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily and reducing blood pressure.
medications.howToUse: Take by mouth once daily, with or without food. Take at the same time each day for best results.
medications.dosage: Adults: Initial dose 10 mg once daily. Usual maintenance dose 20-40 mg once daily. Maximum 80 mg per day.
medications.seriousSideEffects: Severe allergic reactions (swelling of face/tongue/throat). Chest pain or shortness of breath. Fainting or severe dizziness. Seek immediate medical attention.
medications.drugInteractions: Do not combine with other blood pressure medications without doctor approval. NSAIDs may reduce effectiveness. Potassium supplements may cause high potassium levels.
precautions: Do not use if pregnant or planning to become pregnant
Monitor blood pressure regularly
Report persistent dry cough to your doctor
Avoid potassium supplements unless directed by doctor
Do not suddenly stop taking this medication

medications.name: Metformin
medications.description: Metformin is an oral medication that helps control blood sugar levels in people with type 2 diabetes. It works by decreasing glucose production in the liver and improving insulin sensitivity.
medications.howToUse: Take by mouth with food to reduce stomach upset. Swallow tablets whole.
medications.dosage: Adults: 500 mg twice daily initially, may increase to 1000-1500 mg daily. Children: Dosage based on age and weight.
medications.seriousSideEffects: Lactic acidosis (rare but serious). Vitamin B12 deficiency with long-term use. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience difficulty breathing, muscle pain, or unusual tiredness.
medications.drugInteractions: May interact with contrast dyes used in imaging studies. Can affect kidney function medications. Alcohol may increase risk of lactic acidosis.
precautions: Do not use if you have severe kidney disease
Hold medication before surgery or imaging with contrast dye
Monitor kidney function regularly
May cause vitamin B12 deficiency; get levels checked yearly
